title: Nonnegative kinetic density and moment domain

items.title: Nonnegative kinetic density and moment domain
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Adopt Countable Choice, denoted $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval measured in seconds, let $L_1,L_2,L_3>0$ be periods measured in metres, and let
$$\Omega:=\prod_{j=1}^3(\mathbb R/L_j\mathbb Z).$$
Write $C:=\prod_{j=1}^3[0,L_j)$ and let $\pi:\mathbb R^3\to\Omega$ be the quotient map. Define $dx$ on Borel subsets $E\subseteq\Omega$ by
$$dx(E):=\lambda_3(C\cap\pi^{-1}(E)),$$
and use its completion as the spatial measure. Thus $dx$ is the pushforward of three-dimensional Lebesgue measure restricted to the half-open fundamental cell $C$, is not divided by the cell volume, and satisfies $dx(\Omega)=L_1L_2L_3$. Velocity $v\in\mathbb R^3$ is measured in metres per second and $dv$ is three-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Time integration uses Lebesgue measure $dt$ on $I$; product integrals use the corresponding product measures. In this definition $f\,dx\,dv$ is a number count, so a density $f$ has units $\mathrm m^{-3}(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})^{-3}$.

Set $v_*:=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. For $k=2,3$, define the dimensionless polynomial weight $\omega_k(v):=\sum_{j=0}^k(|v|/v_*)^j$. A kinetic density is a finite-valued measurable function $f:I\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ for which, at every $(t,x)$ under discussion,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\omega_3(v)f(t,x,v)\,dv<\infty.$$
Define number density $n:=\int f\,dv$ and mass density $\rho:=mn$ for a fixed particle mass $m>0$ in kilograms. Where $n>0$, define
$$u:=\frac1n\int_{\mathbb R^3}vf\,dv,\qquad c:=v-u,\qquad T:=\frac{m}{3k_Bn}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|c|^2f\,dv,$$
for a fixed Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin. The velocity is $u$ in metres per second and the temperature is $T$ in kelvins. Where also $T>0$, define the candidate monatomic Maxwellian
$$M_{n,u,T}(v):=n\left(\frac{m}{2\pi k_BT}\right)^{3/2} \exp\!\left(-\frac{m|v-u|^2}{2k_BT}\right).$$
Its normalization and moments are established by a separate proposition; this formula is a definition here. At $n=0$, $u$ and $T$ are undefined, and statements using them assume $n>0$. A zero centered second moment gives $T=0$ and does not define the positive-temperature Maxwellian.

Define the pressure tensor, heat-flux vector, and kinetic-energy density by
$$P:=m\int_{\mathbb R^3}c\otimes c\,f\,dv,\qquad q:=\frac m2\int_{\mathbb R^3}|c|^2c\,f\,dv,\qquad E:=\frac m2\int_{\mathbb R^3}|v|^2f\,dv.$$
Here $(a\otimes b)_{ij}=a_i b_j$. The finite absolute third moment makes these integrals finite. Their SI units are respectively pascals, watts per square metre, and joules per cubic metre. This is the monatomic translational model: no internal rotational or vibrational degrees of freedom and no isotropy assumption are included.

references.title: David Tong, Kinetic Theory, Part 2, §§2.2.2–2.4.2, pp. 23–43
François Golse, The Boltzmann Equation and Its Hydrodynamic Limits, §§3.1–3.2, pp. 19–25

items.title: Elastic collision measure and weak collision operator
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Each velocity is in $\mathbb R^3$ measured in metres per second, $dv=\lambda_3$ is three-dimensional Lebesgue measure, and $v_*=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ is the fixed reference speed. The elastic collision set is
$$Q_{m el}:=\{(v,w,v',w')\in\mathbb R^{12}:v+w=v'+w',\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2\},$$
with its relative Borel sigma-algebra. A collision measure is a nonnegative countably additive measure $
u$ on this set, invariant under particle exchange in either pair and under interchange of incoming and outgoing pairs. Symmetry is a model hypothesis; it does not follow merely from the conservation equations.

The collision model declares an input domain $\mathcal D_
u$ contained in the finite-valued, positive, Lebesgue-measurable functions $f:\mathbb R^3	o(0,\infty)$ for which each of the four coordinate evaluations $f(v),f(w),f(v'),f(w')$ on $Q_{m el}$ is $
u$-measurable. For each $f\in\mathcal D_
u$, it supplies a chosen measurable locally integrable representative $Q_
u(f)\in L^1_{m loc}(\mathbb R^3,dv)$. For finite-valued complex Lebesgue-measurable $\varphi$, set
$$A:=f(v)f(w),\qquad B:=f(v')f(w'),\qquad \delta\varphi:=\varphi(v)+\varphi(w)-\varphi(v')-\varphi(w').$$
Let $\mathcal T_f$ be the class of those $\varphi$ for which $\delta\varphi$ is $
u$-measurable and both integrals
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}|\varphi(v)Q_
u(f)(v)|\,dv,\qquad \int_{Q_{m el}}|(B-A)\delta\varphi|\,d
u$$
are finite. For each $f\in\mathcal D_
u$, the model declares a complex linear subspace $\mathcal S_f\subseteq\mathcal T_f$ containing every compactly supported smooth complex-valued velocity test $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$. Require the weak collision identity
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\varphi(v)Q_
u(f)(v)\,dv = rac14\int_{Q_{m el}}(B-A)\delta\varphi\,d
u$$
for every $\varphi\in\mathcal S_f$. For the moment-balance results below, additionally require $1$, $v_1,v_2,v_3$, and $|v|^2$ to lie in $\mathcal S_f$; for the entropy result additionally require $\log(f/f_{m ref})\in\mathcal S_f$, where $f_{m ref}>0$ is a constant reference density with the same units as $f$. Each required membership includes the stated measurability and absolute-convergence conditions. The collision measure and weak identity are adopted mathematical model data; they do not assert a microscopic derivation or that every density and measure admit such an operator. In a physical application, normalize the units of $
u$ so $Q_
u(f)$ has units of $f$ per second; no specific cross-section or measured collision rate is fixed here.

In addition, assume $\int_{I_0}\int_\Omega\int_{\mathbb R^3}\omega_3(v)f(t,x,v)\,dv\,dx\,dt<\infty$ for every compact time interval $I_0\subset I$; this makes the moment densities and fluxes locally integrable in space-time. u$ invariant under particle exchange in either pair and incoming/outgoing interchange, together with the operator $Q_
u$ from the elastic-collision definition. At each $(t,x)$ assume $f(t,x,\cdot)\in\mathcal D_
u$ and $1,v_1,v_2,v_3,|v|^2\in\mathcal S_{f(t,x,\cdot)}$, with the measurability and absolute-convergence conditions of that definition. With $A=f(v)f(w)$, $B=f(v')f(w')$, and $\delta\varphi=\varphi(v)+\varphi(w)-\varphi(v')-\varphi(w')$, assume for each such test that
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\varphi(v)Q_
u(f)(v)\,dv= rac14\int_{Q_{m el}}(B-A)\delta\varphi\,d
u.$$ Suppose pointwise that
$$\partial_t f+v\cdot
abla_x f=Q_
u(f).$$
Set $n:=\int f\,dv$, $ho:=mn$, $u:=n^{-1}\int vf\,dv$, $c:=v-u$, $T:=m(3k_Bn)^{-1}\int|c|^2f\,dv$, $P:=m\int c\otimes c f\,dv$, $q:=(m/2)\int|c|^2c f\,dv$, and $E:=(m/2)\int|v|^2f\,dv$, using the positive constants $m,k_B$ and Lebesgue measure from the kinetic-density definition. Define $(P u)_i:=\sum_jP_{ij}u_j$ and $
abla_x\cdot A$ rowwise for a matrix field $A$. Then on $I	imes\Omega$,
$$\partial_tho+

$$\partial_t(ho u)+

items.title: Conditional periodic kinetic H theorem
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $I$ be an open time interval in seconds and let $\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^3(\mathbb R/L_j\mathbb Z)$, with fixed periods $L_j>0$ in metres. Give $\Omega$ the completed, unnormalised pushforward of Lebesgue measure on $C=\prod_{j=1}^3[0,L_j)$ under the quotient map, as in the kinetic-density definition. Let $f:\Omega\times\mathbb R^3\times I\to(0,\infty)$ be $C^1$ in $(x,t)$ and $C^2$ in $v$, with $v$ measured in metres per second and $f$ in the units assigned by the kinetic-density definition. Fix a constant $f_{\rm ref}>0$ with the same units as $f$. Put $\ell=\log(f/f_{\rm ref})$, $A=f(x,v,t)f(x,w,t)$, and $B=f(x,v',t)f(x,w',t)$. Use the elastic collision set $Q_{\rm el}=\{(v,w,v',w')\in\mathbb R^{12}:v+w=v'+w',\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2\}$ with its relative Borel sigma-algebra and the nonnegative countably additive measure $\nu$ invariant under particle exchange in either pair and incoming/outgoing interchange, together with the weak operator $Q_\nu$ from the elastic-collision definition. Assume for each $t$ that $f$, $f|v|^2$, and $f|\ell|$ are integrable over $\Omega\times\mathbb R^3$. On each compact time interval assume a common integrable envelope in $(x,v)$ for $|(1+\ell)\partial_t f|$; at each $t$ assume $(1+|\ell|)|v\cdot\nabla_x f|$ is integrable over $\Omega\times\mathbb R^3$. In addition, assume
$$f(1+|v|)|\ell|,\quad (1+|\ell|)|\partial_t f|,\quad (1+|\ell|)|v|\,|\nabla_x f|\in L^1(I_0\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^3,dt\,dx\,dv)\quad\text{for every compact time interval }I_0\subset I,$$
where each velocity integral is over all of $\mathbb R^3$, without a velocity cutoff. Thus the entropy density, entropy flux, and differentiation terms are integrable on compact time-space regions. Define
$$D(x,t):=\frac14\int_{Q_{\rm el}}(A-B)\log(A/B)\,d\nu.$$
Assume that $D$ is measurable and locally integrable on $I\times\Omega$, and that for each $t$ its spatial section belongs to $L^1(\Omega)$. At every $(x,t)$ assume $f(x,\cdot,t)\in\mathcal D_\nu$ and $1,\ell(x,\cdot,t)\in\mathcal S_{f(x,\cdot,t)}$, with the measurability and absolute-convergence conditions of the elastic-collision definition. With $\delta\varphi=\varphi(v)+\varphi(w)-\varphi(v')-\varphi(w')$, assume
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\varphi(v)Q_\nu(f)(v)\,dv=\frac14\int_{Q_{\rm el}}(B-A)\delta\varphi\,d\nu$$
for those two tests, and suppose $\partial_t f+v\cdot\nabla_x f=Q_\nu(f)$. Define
$$h(x,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\log(f/f_{\rm ref})\,dv,\qquad J_H(x,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}v f\log(f/f_{\rm ref})\,dv,$$
$$H(t):=\int_\Omega h(x,t)\,dx,\qquad D_{\rm tot}(t):=\int_\Omega D(x,t)\,dx.$$
Then the local entropy balance holds in distributions: for every $\eta\in C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$,
$$\int_I\int_\Omega\bigl(h\,\partial_t\eta+J_H\cdot\nabla_x\eta-D\eta\bigr)\,dx\,dt=0.$$
Moreover, $D(x,t)\ge0$ for almost every $(x,t)$. The periodic global entropy $H$ is differentiable and
$$\frac{dH}{dt}=-D_{\rm tot}(t)\le0.$$
The inequality is conditional on the adopted weak collision identity; it is not a derivation from reversible many-particle mechanics or a kinetic-PDE existence theorem.

references.title: David Tong, Kinetic Theory, Part 2, §2.3, pp. 32–35
François Golse, The Boltzmann Equation and Its Hydrodynamic Limits, §3.2, pp. 23–25

items.title: Full-support collision equilibrium has Maxwellian form
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Fix a time and let $\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^3(\mathbb R/L_j\mathbb Z)$ for periods $L_j>0$ in metres, with the completed unnormalised pushforward $dx$ of Lebesgue measure on $\prod_j[0,L_j)$ as in the kinetic-density definition. Choose a constant reference density $f_{m ref}>0$ with the units of $f$, and let $f:\Omega	imes\mathbb R^3	o(0,\infty)$ be measurable in $x$, $C^2$ in velocity $v\in\mathbb R^3$ measured in metres per second, and integrable in velocity for almost every $x$. Let $Q_{m el}=\{(v,w,v',w')\in\mathbb R^{12}:v+w=v'+w',\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2\}$ with its relative Borel sigma-algebra, and let $
u$ be a locally finite symmetric measure on this set with full support, meaning every nonempty relatively open subset has positive $
u$-measure. Use the collision domain and weak-test spaces of the elastic-collision definition; for almost every $x$, require $f(x,\cdot)\in\mathcal D_
u$, so its four collision evaluations are $
u$-measurable and all compactly supported smooth tests have the required absolute convergence in the weak identity. Define
$$D_x:= rac14\int_{Q_{m el}} igl(f(x,v)f(x,w)-f(x,v')f(x,w') igr) \log\!\left( rac{f(x,v)f(x,w)}{f(x,v')f(x,w')}ight)d
u,$$
and assume $D_x$ is measurable and integrable. If $\int_\Omega D_x\,dx=0$, then for almost every $x$ there exist $C(x)>0$ with the units of $f$, $U(x)\in\mathbb R^3$ measured in metres per second, and $	heta(x)>0$ measured in squared metres per second squared, such that
$$f(x,v)=C(x)\exp\!\left(- rac{|v-U(x)|^2}{2	heta(x)}ight)\quad	ext{for every }v\in\mathbb R^3.$$
For almost every such $x$, the collision operator annihilates this profile in the weak sense that $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\varphi(v)Q_
u(f(x,\cdot))(v)\,dv=0$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$. Conversely, every profile of this form has $D_x=0$; when it belongs to $\mathcal D_
u$, the same compact-test weak identity gives this annihilation conclusion. Here $	heta$ has units of squared speed. The claim characterizes zero collision production only; it does not assert that a spatially varying Maxwellian solves the transport equation.

items.title: Gaussian Maxwellian normalization, stress, and heat flux
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Adopt Countable Choice, denoted $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, as in the kinetic-density definition. Let $n>0$, $u\in\mathbb R^3$, $T>0$, particle mass $m>0$, and Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$. Set $\theta=k_BT/m$ and define $M_{n,u,T}(v):=n(2\pi\theta)^{-3/2}\exp(-|v-u|^2/(2\theta))$. Its Lebesgue moments are
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}M_{n,u,T}\,dv=n,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R^3}vM_{n,u,T}\,dv=nu,$$
$$m\int_{\mathbb R^3}(v-u)\otimes(v-u)M_{n,u,T}\,dv=nk_BT\,I_3,\qquad \frac m2\int_{\mathbb R^3}|v-u|^2(v-u)M_{n,u,T}\,dv=0,$$
and
$$\frac m2\int_{\mathbb R^3}|v|^2M_{n,u,T}\,dv =\frac{mn|u|^2}{2}+\frac{3nk_BT}{2}.$$
Thus its pressure tensor is isotropic and its centered heat flux vanishes; these conclusions concern this Gaussian profile and do not impose isotropy on a general kinetic density.

references.title: David Tong, Kinetic Theory, Part 2, §2.4.2, pp. 40–43
Nicola Zamponi, From the Boltzmann Equation to Hydrodynamic Models, §3.2, pp. 11–12

items.title: Euler equations under weighted local-equilibrium convergence
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $T_*>0$ seconds, let $L_1,L_2,L_3>0$ be fixed spatial periods in metres, and set $\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^3(\mathbb R/L_j\mathbb Z)$. Give $\Omega$ the completed unnormalised pushforward $dx$ of Lebesgue measure on $C=\prod_j[0,L_j)$ under the quotient map, as in the kinetic-density definition. Let $v_*=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. For $k=2,3$ put
$$\omega_k(v):=\sum_{j=0}^k(|v|/v_*)^j.$$
Let $Q_{\rm el}=\{(v,w,v',w')\in\mathbb R^{12}:v+w=v'+w',\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2\}$ be the elastic collision set, and use the nonnegative countably additive symmetric collision measure $\nu$ and operator $Q_\nu:\mathcal D_\nu\to L^1_{\rm loc}$ specified in the earlier elastic-collision definition; the three particle-exchange and incoming/outgoing invariances are hypotheses on $\nu$. Thus, for each $f^\epsilon(x,\cdot,t)$ in its declared collision domain, the weak identity has factor $1/4$ and collision bracket $\delta\psi=\psi(v)+\psi(w)-\psi(v')-\psi(w')$ whenever the test and both integrals are admissible. For each dimensionless $\epsilon>0$, let $f^\epsilon>0$ be periodic, $C^1$ in $(t,x)$ and $C^2$ in $v$ on the closed slab (with one-sided time derivatives at its endpoints), with $\int\omega_3 f^\epsilon\,dv<\infty$ at each $(t,x)$, and solve on $0<t<T_*$
$$\epsilon(\partial_t f^\epsilon+v\cdot\nabla_xf^\epsilon)=Q_\nu(f^\epsilon).$$ Assume the common $L^1(dv)$ derivative envelopes from the moment-balance proposition: for each multiplier $\psi\in\{m,mv_1,mv_2,mv_3,m|v|^2/2\}$, the time derivative and each spatially weighted derivative have one velocity majorant independent of $(t,x)$ on compact time slabs. At every $(t,x)$, require $f^\epsilon(x,\cdot,t)\in\mathcal D_\nu$ and $1,v_1,v_2,v_3,|v|^2\in\mathcal S_{f^\epsilon(x,\cdot,t)}$ with the measurability and absolute-convergence conditions of the elastic-collision definition; assume finite velocity moments through degree three. The elastic bracket of each such invariant is zero. Let $n,u,T$ be $C^1$ on $[0,T_*]\times\Omega$, periodic in $x$, with $n,T$ bounded above and bounded away from zero and $u$ bounded; $n$ is number density in $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, $u$ is velocity in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and $T$ is temperature in kelvins. Use the fixed particle mass $m>0$ in kilograms and Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin from the kinetic-density definition, and define $\rho=mn$, $p=nk_BT$, $E=\rho|u|^2/2+3nk_BT/2$, and
$$M_{n,u,T}(v):=n(2\pi\theta)^{-3/2}e^{-|v-u|^2/(2\theta)},\qquad\theta:=k_BT/m.$$ Assume, as $\epsilon\downarrow0$, that
$$\int_0^{T_*}\!\int_\Omega\!\int_{\mathbb R^3}\omega_3(v)|f^\epsilon-M_{n,u,T}|\,dv\,dx\,dt\longrightarrow0,$$
and
$$\int_\Omega\!\int_{\mathbb R^3}\omega_2(v)|f^\epsilon(0,x,v)-M_{n,u,T}(0,x,v)|\,dv\,dx\longrightarrow0.$$
Then $\rho=mn$, $p=nk_BT$, and $E=\rho|u|^2/2+3nk_BT/2$ satisfy the compressible monatomic Euler equations in distributions on $(0,T_*)\times\Omega$; explicitly, for all scalar test functions $\phi,\eta\in C^1([0,T_*]\times\Omega)$ and vector test function $\zeta\in C^1([0,T_*]\times\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ that are periodic in $x$ and vanish near $t=T_*$ but may be nonzero at $t=0$,
$$\partial_t\rho+\nabla_x\cdot(\rho u)=0,$$
$$\partial_t(\rho u)+\nabla_x\cdot(\rho u\otimes u+pI_3)=0,$$
$$\partial_tE+\nabla_x\cdot((E+p)u)=0,$$
and the corresponding weak identities with the initial traces are
$$\int_0^{T_*}\!\int_\Omega(\rho\,\partial_t\phi+\rho u\cdot\nabla_x\phi)\,dx\,dt+\int_\Omega\rho(0,x)\phi(0,x)\,dx=0,$$
$$\int_0^{T_*}\!\int_\Omega(\rho u\cdot\partial_t\zeta+(\rho u\otimes u+pI_3):\nabla_x\zeta)\,dx\,dt+\int_\Omega\rho(0,x)u(0,x)\cdot\zeta(0,x)\,dx=0,$$
$$\int_0^{T_*}\!\int_\Omega(E\,\partial_t\eta+(E+p)u\cdot\nabla_x\eta)\,dx\,dt+\int_\Omega E(0,x)\eta(0,x)\,dx=0,$$
where $(A:\nabla_x\zeta):=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}\partial_{x_j}\zeta_i$. Their initial traces are the values of these fields at $t=0$. Since the limiting fields are $C^1$, the equations hold pointwise for $0<t<T_*$. This is a conditional passage theorem: it assumes the weighted convergence and asserts no such convergence or kinetic solution exists.

references.title: François Golse, The Boltzmann Equation and Its Hydrodynamic Limits, §§3.1–3.2 (context only)
Nicola Zamponi, From the Boltzmann Equation to Hydrodynamic Models, §3.2, pp. 11–12

items.title: Single-species BGK relaxation operator
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Adopt Countable Choice, denoted $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, as in the kinetic-density definition. Fix the particle mass $m>0$ in kilograms, Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin, and velocity Lebesgue measure $dv$ from the kinetic-density definition. Put $v_*=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $\omega_3(v)=\sum_{j=0}^3(|v|/v_*)^j$. Here $v\in\mathbb R^3$ is measured in metres per second, and $f$ is a number density in velocity space with units $\mathrm{s^3\,m^{-6}}$. For a finite-valued nonnegative measurable velocity density $f:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ with finite absolute third moment $\int\omega_3(v)f(v)\,dv<\infty$, set $n:=\int f\,dv$. Where $n>0$, set $u:=n^{-1}\int vf\,dv$ and $T:=m(3k_Bn)^{-1}\int|v-u|^2f\,dv$; then $n$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, $u$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and $T$ has units kelvins. Define the admissible BGK input domain
$$\mathcal D_{\rm BGK}:=\left\{f:\int\omega_3f\,dv<\infty,\ f\ge0\text{ finite-valued measurable},\ n>0,\ \int|v-u|^2f\,dv>0\right\}.$$
Fix a relaxation time $\tau>0$ measured in seconds. For $f\in\mathcal D_{\rm BGK}$, the temperature $T$ is strictly positive, $\theta:=k_BT/m$ has units $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-2}}$, and the moment-matched Maxwellian $M[f]$ and relaxation operator are defined by the following formulas; $M[f]$ has the same units as $f$:
$$M[f](v):=n(2\pi\theta)^{-3/2}\exp(-|v-u|^2/(2\theta)),\qquad Q_{\rm BGK}(f):=\frac{M[f]-f}{\tau}.$$
The displayed formula defines the single-species Bhatnagar–Gross–Krook (BGK) relaxation operator pointwise on $\mathcal D_{\rm BGK}$, with $Q_{\rm BGK}(f)$ in units of $f$ per second. The corresponding accelerated homogeneous model with dimensionless parameter $\epsilon>0$ is $\partial_t f=Q_{\rm BGK}(f)/\epsilon$. Outside $\mathcal D_{\rm BGK}$ this item assigns no BGK operator. This is a prescribed relaxation model. It is distinct from the binary collision operator and does not by itself assert a derivation from microscopic mechanics or an inhomogeneous hydrodynamic limit.

references.title: David Tong, Kinetic Theory, Part 2, §2.5.1, pp. 45–46
Nicola Zamponi, From the Boltzmann Equation to Hydrodynamic Models, §3.2, pp. 11–12

items.title: Exact homogeneous BGK fast relaxation
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Adopt Countable Choice, denoted $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, as in the kinetic-density definition. Let $v_*=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $\omega_3(v):=\sum_{j=0}^3(|v|/v_*)^j$, let $\tau>0$ be a relaxation time in seconds, and let $\epsilon>0$ be dimensionless. Let $f_0:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ be a finite-valued measurable velocity density with units fixed by the kinetic-density definition, with $\int\omega_3f_0\,dv<\infty$, number density $n>0$, and strictly positive centered second moment. Let $M=M[f_0]$ be its positive-temperature Gaussian from the single-species BGK definition. Fix a constant reference density $f_{\rm ref}>0$ with the same units as $f_0$ and assume $\int f_0|\log(f_0/f_{\rm ref})|\,dv<\infty$, with $0\log0:=0$ and the integrand $f_0|\log(f_0/f_{\rm ref})|$ assigned value zero where $f_0=0$. Define
$$f^\epsilon(t,v):=M(v)+e^{-t/(\epsilon\tau)}(f_0(v)-M(v)),\qquad t\ge0\text{ in seconds}.$$
Then $f^\epsilon\ge0$, has the same mass, momentum, and kinetic energy as $f_0$ for every $t$, belongs to $C^1([0,\infty);L^1(\omega_3\,dv))$, and solves, as an equality in $L^1(\omega_3\,dv)$,
$$\partial_t f^\epsilon=\frac{M[f^\epsilon]-f^\epsilon}{\epsilon\tau},\qquad f^\epsilon(0)=f_0.$$
A solution means a nonnegative $C^1([0,\infty);L^1(\omega_3\,dv))$ function satisfying this equality at each time. The solution is unique among nonnegative solutions in this function class whose density and temperature remain strictly positive. Moreover,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\omega_3|f^\epsilon(t)-M|\,dv =e^{-t/(\epsilon\tau)}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\omega_3|f_0-M|\,dv,$$
and for every $T_*>0$,
$$\int_0^{T_*}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\omega_3|f^\epsilon-M|\,dv\,dt \le\epsilon\tau\int_{\mathbb R^3}\omega_3|f_0-M|\,dv.$$
Thus the equilibrium limit is exact for each fixed $t>0$ and in spacetime weighted $L^1$, but need not be uniform at $t=0$. This branch has stationary homogeneous Euler moments; it gives no evolving inhomogeneous Euler limit.

references.title: David Tong, Kinetic Theory, Part 2, §2.5.1, pp. 45–46
François Golse, The Boltzmann Equation and Its Hydrodynamic Limits, §§3.1–3.2

items.title: Exponential reference-relative entropy bound for homogeneous BGK
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$: every $\mathbb N$-indexed family of nonempty sets has a choice function. Let $v_*=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $\omega_3(v)=\sum_{j=0}^3(|v|/v_*)^j$, let $\tau>0$ be a relaxation time in seconds, and let $\epsilon>0$ be dimensionless. Let $f_0:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ be a finite-valued measurable velocity density with $\int\omega_3 f_0\,dv<\infty$, number density $n=\int f_0\,dv>0$, and strictly positive centered second moment $\int|v-u_0|^2f_0\,dv>0$, where $u_0=n^{-1}\int v f_0\,dv$. Fix a constant reference density $f_{\rm ref}>0$ with the same units as $f_0$, and assume $\int f_0|\log(f_0/f_{\rm ref})|\,dv<\infty$, using $0\log0:=0$ and assigning $f_0|\log(f_0/f_{\rm ref})|$ the value zero where $f_0=0$. These are the hypotheses of the homogeneous BGK relaxation theorem; the fixed $m>0$ and $k_B>0$ and the Gaussian $M=M[f_0]$ are as in the single-species BGK definition. Set
$$f^\epsilon(t)=M+e^{-t/(\epsilon\tau)}(f_0-M),\qquad t\ge0.$$
For each nonnegative velocity density $g$ with the same units as $f_0$ and for which the integral is absolutely finite, define
$$H(g):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}g(v)\log(g(v)/f_{\rm ref})\,dv,\qquad 0\log0:=0.$$
Then for every time $t\ge0$ measured in seconds,
$$0\le H(f^\epsilon(t))-H(M) \le e^{-t/(\epsilon\tau)}\bigl(H(f_0)-H(M)\bigr).$$
The lower bound is relative entropy with respect to the moment-matched Maxwellian. This is a deduction for the adopted BGK model and its explicit solution, not an empirical entropy measurement or a claim about the binary collision operator.

references.title: David Tong, Kinetic Theory, Part 2, §2.5.1, pp. 45–46
François Golse, The Boltzmann Equation and Its Hydrodynamic Limits, §§3.1–3.2

items.title: Restricted collision support need not force Maxwellians
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $v,w,v\prime,w\prime\in\mathbb R^3$ be velocities measured in metres per second, let $dv$ be three-dimensional Lebesgue measure, and set $Q_{m el}:=\{(v,w,v\prime,w\prime):v+w=v\prime+w\prime,\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v\prime|^2+|w\prime|^2\}$. Let $
u$ be a nonnegative countably additive measure on $Q_{m el}$ invariant under exchange of either velocity pair and interchange of incoming and outgoing pairs. For a positive finite-valued Lebesgue-measurable velocity density $g\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ whose four coordinate evaluations on $Q_{m el}$ are $
u$-measurable, set $A_g:=g(v)g(w)$ and $B_g:=g(v\prime)g(w\prime)$, and define the possibly infinite collision entropy production by $\mathscr P_
u(g):= rac14\int_{Q_{m el}}(A_g-B_g)\log(A_g/B_g)\,d
u$. A Maxwellian means a function $C\exp(-|v-U|^2/(2	heta))$ for a density scale $C>0$ with the units of $g$, a velocity $U\in\mathbb R^3$, and squared speed $	heta>0$. Full support means every nonempty relatively open subset of $Q_{m el}$ has positive $
u$-measure. The proposed implication that $\mathscr P_
u(g)=0$ forces $g$ to be Maxwellian for every such symmetric $
u$ and positive integrable $g$ is false without a full-support assumption on $
u$.

François Golse, The Boltzmann Equation and Its Hydrodynamic Limits, §3.2, pp. 23–25

items.title: Non-equilibrium BGK data create an initial layer
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Adopt Countable Choice, denoted $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, as in the kinetic-density definition. Let $v_*=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $\omega_3(v)=\sum_{j=0}^3(|v|/v_*)^j$, $\theta>0$ be a squared speed, choose a speed $a>0$ with $a^2<\theta$, and let $n>0$. For a positive-definite covariance matrix $\Sigma$, define the normalized Gaussian
$$G_{\mu,\Sigma}(v):=\frac{n}{(2\pi)^{3/2}\sqrt{\det\Sigma}} \exp\!\left(-\frac12(v-\mu)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}(v-\mu)\right).$$
Set $\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\theta-a^2,\theta,\theta)$ and
$$f_0(v):=\frac12G_{ae_1,\Sigma}(v)+\frac12G_{-ae_1,\Sigma}(v).$$
This positive density has mass $n$, mean velocity $0$, and normalized covariance $\theta I_3$ (equivalently, second centered moment tensor $n\theta I_3$), so its moment-matched Maxwellian is $M=M_{n,0,T}$ with $k_BT=m\theta$. It is not itself Maxwellian and satisfies $\int f_0|\log(f_0/f_{\rm ref})|\,dv<\infty$ for every fixed positive constant reference density $f_{\rm ref}$ with the same units as $f_0$, interpreting the integrand as zero where $f_0=0$. For $\epsilon,\tau>0$, its homogeneous BGK evolution is
$$f^\epsilon(t,v)=M(v)+e^{-t/(\epsilon\tau)}(f_0(v)-M(v)).$$
For every $t>0$ this approaches $M$ as $\epsilon\to0$, and on every finite interval $[0,T_*]$ its $\omega_3$ weighted spacetime distance to $M$ is at most $\epsilon\tau\int\omega_3|f_0-M|\,dv$. It does not converge uniformly in time on $[0,T_*]$, since the distance at $t=0$ is strictly positive.

references.title: David Tong, Kinetic Theory, Part 2, §2.5.1, pp. 45–46
Nicola Zamponi, From the Boltzmann Equation to Hydrodynamic Models, §3.2, pp. 11–12

items.title: Scope of the kinetic-to-fluid limit results
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: The Euler-passage theorem in this collection assumes weighted strong convergence to local Maxwellians and proves only the resulting conservation-law passage. The separate homogeneous BGK theorem gives an explicit relaxation solution and its limit. Neither result proves convergence for general inhomogeneous Boltzmann solutions, a Boltzmann–Grad limit from deterministic many-particle dynamics, or a Navier–Stokes–Fourier limit. Those questions require additional hypotheses and separate theorem chains.
